transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist here. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Nice to meet you. I suppose what finally got me to make an appointment is that my concentration has just gotten pretty unreliable lately. 

I'll be at the clinic reviewing a patient's chart, or even at home just trying to lay out a watercolor wash, and... well, I'll suddenly realize I've read the same line three times. My mind just completely wanders off to everything that could possibly go wrong. It's just starting to really get in the way of things, and I figured I needed to get it checked out.
When your mind wanders and you lose concentration, are you typically worrying about things or anxious about what might go wrong, or does your attention just drift without that worried feeling?

It's definitely the worrying. It doesn't just drift off peacefully. 

My mind just keeps circling around all sorts of things. I'll start thinking about the clinic—you know, whether my old patients are being looked after properly as I step back, or if the financial side of the practice handoff is actually sound. And then it shifts to... well, whether I’ll just become completely useless once I’m fully retired. 

It just keeps going from one thing to the next. And honestly, the amount of worry feels out of proportion even to me, but I just can't seem to shut it off.
How long has this constant worrying and difficulty concentrating been going on?
Well, it's been going on for a while now. I'd say... it really started when I began the formal retirement process. So, that would be about a year and three months ago.
Beyond the worry and concentration problems, have you noticed changes in your mood—like feeling down, empty, or depressed—over this past year or so?

No, I wouldn't say I've felt depressed or empty. It's really just this constant state of being on edge. I mean, I don't feel down or hopeless, I just feel... wound up all the time. My mood is generally okay, as long as I'm not actively spiraling about something going wrong. So, no, not depressed. Just overly worried.
